items.title: Nine People Cling to Capsized Boat in Rough Lake Ontario Waters Off Port Credit
items.summary: According to the Toronto Star, Peel police rescued nine people Saturday evening after their boat capsized in rough conditions near Port Credit Harbour Marina in Mississauga. Const. Tyler Bell-Morena, a Peel police spokesperson, told the Toronto Star that officers found the vessel flipped over roughly 50 metres south of the Ridgetown break wall, tossed by high winds and waves reaching two to three metres. Bell-Morena described the conditions as challenging, and said all nine people were found clinging to the overturned boat when officers arrived. The Toronto Star reports everyone involved suffered only minor abrasions, with no other injuries reported. Investigators said it remains unclear what type of boat was involved. Bell-Morena said the vessel was later located near rocks on the west side of the Credit River, but crews were unable to recover it because of hazardous weather conditions. The Canadian Coast Guard was notified of the incident, the Toronto Star reports.

items.title: New AGM Exhibition Turns One Artist's Family Archives Into a Story of Displacement
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, the Art Gallery of Mississauga is opening a new exhibition this Saturday that draws directly on one artist's family archives to explore displacement and memory. The show, titled Electric Neon Clock, comes from artist Kobayashi, who used personal family records to examine the forced incarceration and dispossession of Japanese Canadians during the Second World War. Mississauga.com reports the exhibition was curated by the gallery's senior curator, Shannon Anderson, and pairs visual art with a live performance component. Opening day includes a community launch and reception alongside an origami boat workshop, held in partnership with Japan Festival Canada. Gallery organizers describe the show as an immersive experience intended to give visitors a closer look at Japanese Canadian history and culture. Mississauga.com notes the exhibit gives Mississauga residents a chance to engage with a chapter of Canadian history that isn't always widely taught, told through documents drawn from one family's own past.

items.title: Lithium-Ion Batteries Are Now Mississauga's Fastest-Growing Fire Risk, Fire Crews Say
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, Mississauga Fire and Emergency Services has identified lithium-ion batteries as the city's fastest-growing ignition source, recording a 122 per cent jump in battery-related fires in 2025 compared to the year before. The city says MFES responded to 20 lithium-ion battery incidents in 2025 and has already responded to 15 so far this year. Officials note these batteries power everyday devices like cell phones, laptops, e-bikes and power tools, and are generally safe when used properly, but damaged, defective or improperly charged batteries can pose a serious fire risk. The City of Mississauga explains that damaged batteries can sometimes undergo thermal runaway, a chain reaction that produces intense heat, fire, toxic gases and, in some cases, explosions. MFES is urging residents to follow safe charging, storage and disposal practices, and to stop using a battery or device immediately if they notice warning signs such as swelling, unusual odours, excessive heat, discolouration, leaking fluid, smoke, vapour or strange noises. The city adds that anyone whose battery catches fire should move away from it and call 911.

items.title: Crombie and Parrish tied in Mississauga mayoral race: poll
items.summary: A new survey of Mississauga residents finds Bonnie Crombie and Carolyn Parrish are currently tied in the race for mayor. If a mayoral election were held today, incumbent Parrish and former mayor Crombie would each receive 35 per cent among decided and leaning voters, followed by councillors Dipika Damerla at 18 per cent and Alvin Tedjo at 12 per cent, according to a new Liaison Strategies Mississauga survey. Among all voters, Parrish and Crombie are tied at 26 per cent each, followed by Damerla at 13 per cent and Tedjo at nine per cent. Twenty-six per cent are undecided, Liaison Strategies said. “The more important number may be undecided,” said David Valentin, principal at Liaison Strategies. ” The numbers have changed compared with the Liaison Strategies October Mississauga poll, when Crombie led Parrish 38 per cent to 33 per cent, Tedjo was at 12 per cent, and Damerla was at 7 per cent, said Valentin. “So the story is not simply that the statistical tie between Crombie and Parrish continues,” he said. ” As of Aug. 14, there were 10 candidates registered for the mayoral race in Mississauga. Frank Fang, who ran in the 2024 mayoral byelection in Mississauga; David Shaw, who ran in both the 2024 mayoral byelection and the 2022 municipal election for mayor; Mike Matulewicz who ran in 2024 mayoral byelection; Fadi Naami and Amjad Jilani were registered as of Aug. 14.

items.title: Ford's Backing of Parrish for Mississauga Mayor May Be Working Against Her, New Poll Suggests
items.summary: According to the Toronto Star, a new Liaison Strategies poll suggests Mississauga Mayor Carolyn Parrish and former mayor Bonnie Crombie are locked in a dead heat heading into the fall election, even though Ontario Premier Doug Ford has publicly backed Parrish's campaign. The poll, released Friday, found Parrish and Crombie would each take 26 per cent of the vote if the Oct. 26 election were held today, with another 26 per cent of voters still undecided. Councillors Dipika Damerla and Alvin Tedjo trailed with 13 per cent and nine per cent respectively, according to the poll. The Star reports Liaison principal David Valentin said none of the candidates has made a clear case for why voters should choose them over the others, leaving a large pool of undecided voters still up for grabs amid a broader sense the city is heading in the wrong direction. The Star notes an October 2025 Liaison poll also found Crombie and Parrish tied in a then-hypothetical matchup, before Crombie left to lead the Ontario Liberals and later resigned after the party's provincial election loss. Candidate registration for the fall municipal elections opened Friday as well.

items.title: Russia’s bid to free plane at Toronto Pearson Airport rejected by Canadian judge
items.summary: A massive Russian cargo plane that has been stranded at Toronto Pearson Airport in Mississauga for more than four years is staying put after a Federal Court judge rejected the aircraft owner’s latest attempt to challenge Canadian sanctions. The Antonov An-124, one of the world’s largest cargo aircraft, has been grounded at Pearson since February 2022, shortly after Russia invaded Ukraine and Canada closed its airspace to Russian-owned aircraft. The Canadian government subsequently seized the plane on June 8, 2023, as part of its sanctions against Russia. Ottawa has said it wants to eventually transfer the aircraft to Ukraine as part of Canada’s support for the country. Now, the legal fight over the plane’s future continues. Volga Dnepr Airlines, Russia’s largest air cargo carrier and the registered owner of the aircraft, asked the Federal Court to review the federal government’s decision to maintain sanctions against the company and its former chairman. The airline had applied in 2023 to be removed from Canada’s sanctions list, arguing that it had refused to carry military cargo since 2018. The federal government rejected the request, saying the airline has benefited from Russian government contracts and subsidies and has helped Russian President Vladimir Putin’s regime circumvent sanctions. The judge has now rejected the company’s bid for sanctions relief.
